definition: The IBM Shoebox was a 1961 IBM computer that was able to perform mathematical functions and provide speech recognition.
details: It was capable of recognizing 16 spoken words, including the digits from 0 through 9. It was developed by William C. Dersch in the Advanced Systems Development Division Laboratory at IBM
story: Imagine learning a language by reading every book in the library and noticing, over time, which words travel together. It does not memorize a rulebook; it absorbs a library. The machine learns language the way you did — by hearing so much of it that the patterns sink in. It is fluency built from pattern, not from memorized rules. That pattern-earned fluency is IBM Shoebox.
